verses.commentary: Do not rejoice, Israel. Joy forbidden. Do not be jubilant like other nations. No celebration. You have been unfaithful. The charge again. You love the wages of a prostitute at every threshing floor. Harvest festivals corrupted by fertility religion.
Threshing floors and winepresses will not feed the people. Agricultural failure. The new wine will fail them. The celebration they expected will not come.
They will not remain in the Lord's land. Exile announced. Ephraim will return to Egypt. The exodus reversed. And eat unclean food in Assyria. Dietary law impossible in foreign land.

They will not pour out wine offerings to the Lord. Worship impossible. Their sacrifices will be like the bread of mourners. Ritually contaminated. All who eat will be unclean. The whole meal defiled. It will not come into the temple of the Lord. Cut off from proper worship.
What will you do on the day of your appointed festivals? The festivals they corrupted will become festivals they cannot keep. Religious calendar emptied.
Even if they escape destruction, Egypt will gather them. Refugees fleeing to Egypt. Memphis will bury them. They will die there. Treasures of silver taken over by briers. Wealth abandoned, overgrown.

The days of punishment are coming. Reckoning at hand. Let Israel know this. Awareness demanded. The prophet is considered a fool. How they treat God's messenger. The inspired person a maniac. Madness attributed to those with God's word.
The prophet is the watchman over Ephraim. Hosea's role defined. Yet snares await him on all his paths. The messenger is hunted. Hostility in the house of his God. Opposition even in sacred space.
They have sunk deep into corruption. How far they have fallen. As in the days of Gibeah. The worst period of the judges (Judges 19-21). God will remember their wickedness. Punishment coming.

When I found Israel, it was like finding grapes in the desert. A joyful discovery. Like early fruit on the fig tree. Promising beginnings. But when they came to Baal Peor. The turning point (Numbers 25). They became as vile as the thing they loved. Worship shapes worshipers.
Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird. Glory departing. No birth, no pregnancy, no conception. The sequence reversed. Fertility cursed at every stage.
Even if they rear children, I will bereave them of every one. Those born will be lost. Woe to them when I turn away. The ultimate judgment is God's withdrawal.
I have seen Ephraim like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. Beautiful positioning. But Ephraim will bring out their children to the slayer. The pleasant place produces victims.
Give them, Lord, what will you give them? The prophet prays. Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that are dry. A terrible prayer. Better not to be born than to be born into judgment.

Because of all their wickedness in Gilgal. The site of coronation and corruption. I hated them there. Strong word. I will drive them out of my house. Eviction from God's presence. I will love them no longer. Love withdrawn. All their leaders are rebellious. Comprehensive failure.
Ephraim is blighted, their root is withered. Dead from below. They yield no fruit. Barren. Even if they bear children, I will slay their cherished offspring. Nothing escapes.
My God will reject them. Hosea speaks. Because they have not obeyed him. The reason clear. They will be wanderers among the nations. No home, no rest. The curse of Cain extended to a nation.
